segments.title: End of day one and opening of day two
segments.summary: Brown confirms he was in Miles's band by November 1968 and the tape ends; day two starts on November 11.

segments.chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
segments.title: Studio method for In a Silent Way and Bitches Brew
segments.summary: Miles keeps the tape rolling in the old Columbia church studio, giving sketches and grooves that Teo Macero edits.

segments.chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
segments.title: Studio versus live tempos and trust in Miles's band
segments.summary: Miles's live versions are faster, he relied on thinking musicians, and Chick Corea picks up his trumpet one night.

segments.chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
segments.title: Chick Corea on trumpet and Pat Metheny's trumpet roots
segments.summary: Chats about Chick's trumpet and drumming and how Miles listened from the side while Chick and Dave went to extremes.

segments.chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
segments.title: The electric period, the Lost Quintet and bootlegs
segments.summary: Miles adds electric instruments; a bootleg of "Milestones" at Juan-les-Pins; Keith Jarrett and Steve Grossman join.

segments.chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
segments.title: Chick and Dave leave, Keith joins, Michael Henderson and the Cellar Door
segments.summary: Chick and Dave go off to form Circle, Miles moves toward electric funk, and the band plays Isle of Wight and the Cellar Door.

segments.chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
segments.title: Live Evil and Miles singing the beat for "What I Say"
segments.summary: He loves Live Evil's grungy electric sound and describes Miles tapping out the rhythm for "What I Say".

segments.chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
segments.title: Airto joins and why Miles moved forward
segments.summary: Airto's organic percussion, the busier music, and DeJohnette's defence of Miles against charges of selling out.

segments.chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
segments.title: How Miles communicated sketches in the studio
segments.summary: Miles brought scales, melodies and bass ostinatos, such as "It's About Time" and "Guinevere", but not whole pieces.

segments.chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
segments.title: Live repertoire and European bootleg recordings
segments.summary: They discuss pieces the band played on tour, like "Masqualero" and "Miss Mabry", and the live Miles releases.

segments.chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
segments.title: Three drummers and percussion on Bitches Brew
segments.summary: How he, Lenny White and Don Alias shared the kit and percussion, including Alias's groove on "Miles Runs the Voodoo Down".

segments.chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
segments.title: Leaving Miles Davis in 1970
segments.summary: He wanted a change and more freedom, as Miles wanted more specific grooves from the drums.

segments.chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
segments.title: Isle of Wight Festival with Miles
segments.summary: Arriving by helicopter, hearing Joni Mitchell, and Miles playing to a huge crowd.

segments.chapter: CTI, Compost and the first Directions
segments.title: Recording at Rudy Van Gelder's for CTI, and touring Europe
segments.summary: CTI sessions in Van Gelder's studio, the CTI stable of players and a tour during the 1972 Munich Olympics.

segments.chapter: CTI, Compost and the first Directions
segments.title: Creed Taylor's influence, Milt Jackson and Ray Brown
segments.summary: Creed's say on session players, CTI concerts, and a night playing with Ray Brown.

segments.chapter: CTI, Compost and the first Directions
segments.title: Forming the co-op band Compost
segments.summary: With Bob Moses, Jack Gregg, Harold Vick and Juma Santos, a tape sent to London leads to a Columbia deal via Yes's manager.

segments.chapter: CTI, Compost and the first Directions
segments.title: Compost's gigs, Lee Morgan's death and the Columbia records
segments.summary: An opening slot for Yes on the night Lee Morgan was shot; without money for touring the band folds after two records.

segments.chapter: CTI, Compost and the first Directions
segments.title: Founding Directions: The Cosmic Chicken, Keystone Korner and Sorcery
segments.summary: He forms the Directions band with Abercrombie, Peter Warren and Alex Foster, records Cosmic Chicken, meets Bobby McFerrin and makes Sorcery at home.

segments.chapter: CTI, Compost and the first Directions
segments.title: Sorcery details and the experimental home recording
segments.summary: He plays organ and C-melody sax on Sorcery, recorded in his living room in 1974.

segments.chapter: CTI, Compost and the first Directions
segments.title: How Compost got its name
segments.summary: The band chose Compost because good things grow from it, like their mix of jazz, rock and soul.

segments.chapter: ECM and the Directions bands
segments.title: Have You Heard? recorded in Tokyo
segments.summary: A Japanese drum tour leads to a Pioneer-sponsored record with Gary Peacock and Benny Maupin.

segments.chapter: ECM and the Directions bands
segments.title: Playing on Alice Coltrane's Universal Consciousness
segments.summary: He recalls recording at the Coltranes' Queens house studio.

segments.chapter: ECM and the Directions bands
segments.title: Chronology and the philosophy behind the name Directions
segments.summary: Directions suited his eclectic music.

segments.chapter: ECM and the Directions bands
segments.title: Ruta and Daitya: the duet with Keith Jarrett and Manfred Eicher
segments.summary: A three-hour Los Angeles studio session with Keith is sent to Manfred Eicher, who releases it on ECM.

segments.chapter: ECM and the Directions bands
segments.title: ECM and the album Untitled
segments.summary: His first ECM band record, its compositions, a C-melody sax, reggae influence and his ties with Eicher.

segments.chapter: ECM and the Directions bands
segments.title: New Directions with Lester Bowie, Abercrombie and Eddie Gomez
segments.summary: The Directions band changes into New Directions, one of his favorite groups.

segments.chapter: ECM and the Directions bands
segments.title: Clearing up when he first played with Lester Bowie
segments.summary: Brown checks the biography: he knew of Bowie in Chicago but first played with him in New York.

segments.chapter: Special Edition
segments.title: Special Edition: Zoot Suite and Journey to the Twyn Planet
segments.summary: Inspired by Arthur Blythe and David Murray, he writes music and plays electric melodica; pieces include Zoot Suite and the Twyn Planet dream.

segments.chapter: Special Edition
segments.title: Central Park West, One For Eric and Eric Dolphy
segments.summary: Discussion of the Coltrane ballad and his tribute to Dolphy, whom he only heard live in Chicago.

segments.chapter: Special Edition
segments.title: Special Edition personnel changes
segments.summary: Peter Warren is replaced by Rufus Reid and horns come and go, with drum machines and synthesizers.

segments.chapter: Special Edition
segments.title: Bernard Purdie and The Hitmaker
segments.summary: He admires Purdie's reading and grooves.

segments.chapter: Special Edition
segments.title: Pat Metheny's 80/81 band
segments.summary: The ECM date with Metheny, Dewey Redman, Michael Brecker and Charlie Haden and the tours.

segments.chapter: Special Edition
segments.title: Jaco Pastorius's Word of Mouth
segments.summary: He recalls the all-star session under Jaco's direction.

segments.chapter: Special Edition
segments.title: Tin Can Alley, "Gri Gri Man" and Manfred's encouragement
segments.summary: Overdubbed piano, organ and congas, and spontaneous pieces encouraged by Manfred Eicher.

segments.chapter: Special Edition
segments.title: Von Freeman, Fathers and Sons, Fred Anderson and the Chicago connection
segments.summary: Playing with Von Freeman at the Jazz Showcase and on Fathers and Sons, and memories of Fred Anderson.

segments.chapter: Woodstock, MCA and the Standards Trio
segments.title: The Creative Music Studio in Woodstock
segments.summary: Karl Berger's school, its teachers, and a benefit concert recorded in 1981.

segments.chapter: Woodstock, MCA and the Standards Trio
segments.title: Moving to the Woodstock area and having the house built
segments.summary: They moved upstate in the early 1970s, rented in Mt. Tremper, and then had a simple house built from scratch.

segments.chapter: Woodstock, MCA and the Standards Trio
segments.title: Inflation Blues, "Ebony" and the Bratislava jam
segments.summary: The 1982 Special Edition record, a Compost-era piece reworked with ska horns, Ahmad Jamal covering "Ebony", and a 1983 festival jam.

segments.chapter: Woodstock, MCA and the Standards Trio
segments.title: The Zebra soundtrack with Lester Bowie
segments.summary: He writes and programs drum machine and synth music for a Japanese photographer's zebra film, with African and Pygmy-inspired rhythms.

segments.chapter: Woodstock, MCA and the Standards Trio
segments.title: MCA and the Special Edition album Irresistible Forces
segments.summary: The MCA deal via Ricky Schultz and the new band with Greg Osby, Gary Thomas and Nana Vasconcelos, with tunes for Herbie and Milton Nascimento.

segments.chapter: Woodstock, MCA and the Standards Trio
segments.title: Forming the Standards Trio with Keith Jarrett and Gary Peacock
segments.summary: After Gary Peacock's record, Manfred Eicher suggests a trio using standards as vehicles; a Vanguard week leads to Standards and Changes.

segments.chapter: Woodstock, MCA and the Standards Trio
segments.title: Parallel Realities with Herbie Hancock and Pat Metheny
segments.summary: Late-1980s projects including Real Time with Sonny Rollins, and the sequenced, bass-less Parallel Realities record and world tour.

segments.chapter: Woodstock, MCA and the Standards Trio
segments.title: Earthwalk, Blue Note and Michael Cain
segments.summary: He leaves MCA for Blue Note via EMI Japan; Michael Cain joins and pieces include Earthwalk and Monk's Plum.

segments.chapter: Soundtracks and Music for the Fifth World
segments.title: Soundtrack work: Lemon Sky and Herbie Hancock's Blow Up
segments.summary: He plays on Pat Metheny's score for a PBS play and recalls the unused Blow Up music.

segments.chapter: Soundtracks and Music for the Fifth World
segments.title: Soundtrack for City Farmers
segments.summary: He scores a documentary on New York's community gardens and laments their removal.

segments.chapter: Soundtracks and Music for the Fifth World
segments.title: Talking Drummers with Don Alias
segments.summary: Duo percussion music with Don Alias that remains unreleased.

segments.chapter: Soundtracks and Music for the Fifth World
segments.title: Native American interests and the wolf in the clouds
segments.summary: He and Lydia attend powwows, see a wolf-shaped cloud and meet people who lead them to Grandma Twylah.

segments.chapter: Soundtracks and Music for the Fifth World
segments.title: Grandma Twylah, the Wolf Clan and the concept of Music for the Fifth World
segments.summary: They are initiated into the Wolf Clan and he builds the record around her creation story and chants.

segments.chapter: Soundtracks and Music for the Fifth World
segments.title: Recording Fifth World with Living Colour's Will Calhoun
segments.summary: Two guitars and two drummers, chants with Joan Henry and Denis Yerry, and a drum duel at the end.

segments.chapter: Soundtracks and Music for the Fifth World
segments.title: Pieces for Miles and Jim Pepper, and the Fifth World's reception
segments.summary: He writes "Miles" after Miles's death, plays "Witchi-Tai-To" after Pepper dies, and regrets the label did not know how to promote it.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: The Alligator Blues Band in Blues Brothers 2000
segments.summary: He is invited to appear in the film's all-star band battle and recalls the cast.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: Grammy nominations and Ivey Divey with Don Byron and Jason Moran
segments.summary: Two 2004 nominated records, and the bass-less trio concept of Ivey Divey.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: The history of drumming on "Last Chance Stomp"
segments.summary: He recalls changing his sound across eras on The Cosmic Chicken.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: The Latin Project and the Trio Beyond
segments.summary: The Montreal residency produces a Latin group, and Trio Beyond with Larry Goldings and John Scofield honors Tony Williams's Lifetime.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: Oneness and Dancing With Nature Spirits
segments.summary: His ECM Oneness group with Michael Cain, Don Alias and Jerome Harris, and a record with flutist Steve Gorn.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: Extra Special Edition with Bobby McFerrin
segments.summary: A 1994 experimental Special Edition record with guests Paul Grassi and McFerrin.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: Founding his Golden Beams label
segments.summary: Lydia and Minya help him start his own label for archival and unusual projects.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: Music in the Key of Om and Hearts of the Masters with Foday Musa Suso
segments.summary: A meditation recording nominated for a Grammy and a duo record with Suso made at his studio.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: Designing resonating bells with Sabian
segments.summary: He explains the tuned bells made with Sabian and their healing sound, and the Grammy nomination.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: Hybrids, The Ripple Effect and Ben Surman's remixes
segments.summary: His son-in-law remixes their recordings and the ensemble tours with a Roland Handsonic.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: The Elephant Sleeps But Still Remembers with Bill Frisell
segments.summary: A 2000 Seattle concert with Frisell is later enhanced by Ben Surman and released.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: Saudades and Grammy recognition across genres
segments.summary: The Trio Beyond live record is nominated; he is unlikely to tour as a new-age artist.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: Peace Time and its use in hospitals
segments.summary: The Grammy-winning relaxation album with Ben Surman, played in hospitals, released through Koch/E1.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: Music We Are with John Patitucci and Danilo Perez
segments.summary: A co-led trio record and DVD with a sold-out Blue Note week.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: How the 70th-birthday record came about
segments.summary: With Chuck Mitchell's support and the NEA award, he plans a special record with a hand-picked cast and producer Bob Sadin.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: The pieces on the new record Sound Travels
segments.summary: Groove-based compositions with Esperanza Spalding, Ambrose Akinmusire, Bruce Hornsby and Bobby McFerrin.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: Touring plans, the Jack DeJohnette Group and Lydia as business adviser
segments.summary: His current band, a digital live release and plans for the NEA ceremony and a Blue Note night.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: Receiving the NEA Jazz Masters award
segments.summary: He says it took time to sink in and is honored to be recognized.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: His contribution to drumming and music as healing
segments.summary: Brown asks about his legacy; DeJohnette speaks of music as organic, spiritual and tied to everyday life.

segments.chapter: The 2000s, Golden Beams and reflections
segments.title: Closing thanks
segments.summary: Brown thanks DeJohnette on behalf of the Smithsonian and NEA.
